verdicts.summary: Validates; 10 events spot-checked, 9 confirmed, 1 mis-dated at confidence 2 (Erzurum 1192, fixed to 1202). Reviewer applied 3 small fixes. Left for a gap-filler: Sinop held by Trebizond 1254-1265 (Trebizond dossier, confidence 3) and the 1150-1151 Rum gains from the County of Edessa are missing; the 1188 gain and the 1202 western jump are undated (page budget).

fixes.what: Erzurum gain dated 1192 from the Saltukids, but the Rum page says Tughril got Elbistan in 1192 and was installed in Erzurum only once it 'was taken from the Saltukids' at the start of the 13th century.
fixes.why: Sultanate of Rum page: 'Elbistan was given to Tughril ibn Kılıç Arslan II, but when Erzurum was taken from the Saltukids' ... at the start of the 13th century; the note's quote 'Tughril received Erzurum ... 1192' runs two sentences together. Cliopatria adds Erzurum in 1202.
fixes.fix: Year 1192 -> 1202, region text and note rewritten (confidence 2 kept).

fixes.what: The 1192 shape was adjusted to add Erzurum from 1192; with the event re-dated it must stand as drawn.
fixes.why: Same Rum page sentence; Cliopatria's 1202 shape already holds Erzurum.
fixes.fix: Verdict adjust -> ok, correction removed, note rewritten.

fixes.what: Suleiman ibn Qutalmish starts in 1075, before the state's start (1077).
fixes.why: Check 2: rulers must lie inside the life. The ruler's own note gives 1075-1077 as de facto rule before the 1077 secession (infobox 'Division from the Seljuk Empire: 1077').
fixes.fix: from 1075 -> 1077, with the 1075 date kept in the note.

fixes.what: The Rum-Nicaea war (1206-1211) had no zones although Antalya changed hands and a battle was fought at Antioch on the Meander.
fixes.why: Kaykhusraw I page: 'Kaykhusraw seized Antalya in 1207 from its Niceaen garrison'; 'Kaykhusraw was killed at the Battle of Antioch on the Meander in 1211'. The nicaean-empire dossier has the 1211 Meander contest.
fixes.fix: Zones added: Antalya (40 km) and Antioch on the Meander (28.3 E 37.87 N, 40 km).

fixes.what: Missing: the loss of Sinop to Trebizond in 1254 and its recovery in 1265.
fixes.why: empire-of-trebizond /ledger/20 (1254-06 gain sultanate-of-rum, Sinop, confidence 3) and /ledger/21 (1265 loss to sultanate-of-rum). The Rum page does not mention it (checked), so this is a cross-dossier gap, not a fault the author could see within the budget.
fixes.fix: Gap-filler: open 'Empire of Trebizond' or 'Sinop, Turkey'; add 1254 loss empire-of-trebizond {place Sinop, 60 km} and 1265 gain empire-of-trebizond (counterpart, years and land as the page gives), or tell eu-05 why not.

fixes.what: Missing: Mesud I's gains from the County of Edessa in 1150-1151, although county-of-edessa names sultanate-of-rum as a successor.
fixes.why: County of Edessa page: the lands 'were conquered by Nur ad-Din and the Sultan of Rum within a year'; Joscelin II page: 'mostly absorbed by Mesud, Timurtash of Mardin, and Nur ad-Din'. Rum's 1147-1176 shapes stop at 35.9 E and carry none of the county.
fixes.fix: Gap-filler: open 'Mesud I' or 'Kilij Arslan II' for the places (Kesoun, Behesni, Raban, Marash) and add a 1150/1151 gain from county-of-edessa; otherwise county-of-edessa must drop sultanate-of-rum as a successor.

thin.what is missing: 1188 gain (Kayseri and the west to Dorylaeum/Afyon) is confidence 1, unattributed; byzantine-empire /ledger/139 records it as a 1188 loss to Rum (Phrygia, confidence 1).
The 1202 shape's jump west to 27.6 E (Kastamonu and the Phrygian west) has no ledger event (unverified: page budget).
1260 loss to mongol-empire is confidence 1 (extent bridged to the 1305 core); no Mongol mirror.
End of Trebizond's vassalage (1243) is confidence 1.
Sinop lost to Trebizond 1254, regained 1265 (see fixes).
Rum's share of the County of Edessa (see fixes).

verdicts.summary: Validates; 7 events spot-checked, all confirmed in year and place; the 1191 Bagras counterpart was wrong (fixed). Infobox 40,000 km2 (13th c.) against 59,469 km2 (1250 shape): ratio 1.49, acknowledged. Confidence-1 bridges and unnamed Mamluk cessions are recorded under thin, within the 9-page budget.

fixes.what: Bagras (1191) was taken from Saladin's garrison, not from the Knights Templar.
fixes.why: War of the Antiochene Succession: 'In 1191, Leo captured and restored Bagras, a strategically important fortress previously taken by Saladin' (from the Templars); 'Bohemond demanded its return to the Templars, but Leo refused'. The note's 'the 1192 peace confirmed his control' is not on the page: the peace is undated.
fixes.fix: counterpart 'Knights Templar (Bagras)' -> 'ayyubid-sultanate'; note rewritten with the page's words.

fixes.what: The Mamluk invasions war (1266-1303) had empty zones without saying why, though fortresses were ceded in 1285.
fixes.why: Cilicia page: 'The Armenians were obligated to cede many fortresses to the Mamluks' (names not given); 'Hromkla was also sacked' (not annexed).
fixes.fix: Note appended: zones empty because no page names the ceded places.

thin.what is missing: Thoros II's first conquests after 1141 (Vahka, Amouda) are confidence 1, undated.
Recovery of Tarsus, Adana and Anazarbus (Cliopatria 1147-1151) is confidence 1.
Leo I's Isaurian conquests and the reach to 30.6 E (1192 shape) are confidence 1, undated.
1260 western loss to the Karamanids is confidence 1 (decade only); Gaban and Hajin fall inside the removed area although the page keeps them Armenian to 1375.
1260 eastern gain (Marash, Behesni 'recovered in the 1250s') is confidence 1 and unattributed; it came from Rum, whose ledger has no mirror.
Lands ceded after Mari (1266-1268) and in the 1285 truce, and the loss of Ayas (1337) and Silifke, are undated or unnamed.

verdicts.summary: Validates; 7 events spot-checked, 6 confirmed, 1 not dated by its page (1150 sale, confidence lowered to 1). Reviewer fixed two double-counted regions. Left for a gap-filler: the 1150-1151 ending is inconsistent (the whole remnant is lost to Byzantium in 1150 while the 1147 shape stands 'ok' to 1151 and the county dissolves in 1151) and the 1111 and 1126 growth are confidence-1 bridges (5-page budget).

fixes.what: The 1111 gain took the whole 1111-minus-1099 strip, Raban and Kesoun included, which /ledger/5 gains again in 1116.
fixes.why: The dossier's own /keyframe_review/2 correction removes Raban and Kaisun for 1111-1115; Baldwin II page: 'forced his prisoner to renounce Raban and Kaisun in 1116'.

fixes.what: The December 1144 loss took all land east of the Euphrates, Saruj included, which /ledger/11 loses again in January 1145.
fixes.why: Siege of Edessa (1144) page: Zengi took Saruj in January 1145.
fixes.fix: Region now (1139 minus 1147) minus Saruj (38.43 E 36.98 N, 20 km).

fixes.what: The 1150 sale to Manuel I has no year on its page.
fixes.why: County of Edessa page: 'His wife sold Turbessel and what was left of the county to the Byzantine Emperor Manuel I Comnenus', no year; the Joscelin II page gives none either (only the spring-1150 capture).
fixes.fix: Confidence 2 -> 1, note says the year is inferred.

fixes.what: Not blocking: the 1150 loss hands the whole 1147 shape to byzantine-empire, but /keyframe_review/7 keeps that shape 'ok' to 1151, the capital Turbessel runs to 1151 and the dissolve is 1151 with the same region. byzantine-empire has no 1150 gain.
fixes.why: Check 4: a large event with no trace in the keyframes. Joscelin II page: Turbessel held out under Joscelin III and 'fell to Nur ad-Din's captain Hassan in 1151'; the County page infobox has Turbessel the capital '1146–1150'.
fixes.fix: Choose one: (a) end the county in 1150 (end, dissolve, Turbessel to 1150, keyframe 7 adjust 'valid 1147-1150') and ask eu-05 for a 1150 gain and a 1151 loss; or (b) keep 1151, drop the 1150 loss and put the sale in the dissolve note, the successors keeping byzantine-empire as a paper heir.

fixes.what: Not blocking: sultanate-of-rum is listed as a successor, but the Rum dossier has no gain from county-of-edessa and its shapes never reach the county.
fixes.why: Check 9: successors must carry land and agree with the neighbour's dossier (sultanate-of-rum, this batch).
fixes.fix: Keep it and have Rum add the 1150-1151 gain (see the sultanate-of-rum fixes), or drop it.
